title: Current practices and future direction of artificial intelligence in mathematics education: A systematic review
venue: International Electronic Journal of Mathematics Education
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the growing use of artificial intelligence in mathematics education and the need for a practical synthesis of how AI is being used, at which educational levels, and through which specific tools. The review is motivated by the observation that prior reviews often discussed broad AI categories but did not sufficiently identify ready-to-use or commercialized tools that educators could adopt in practice.

The intervention studied is not a single program but the broader landscape of AI tools and applications in mathematics education. Using a systematic literature review of articles from Web of Science and Scopus published between 2019 and 2024, the authors analyzed 32 studies. They categorized AI tools used in mathematics education into chatbots, virtual reality, augmented reality, adaptive learning systems/intelligent tutoring systems, learning analytics, serious games, and AI mathematics problem solvers. They also identified commercialized tools such as ChatGPT, Bard, GeoGebra AR, Khan Academy, Squirrel AI, Photomath, and others, and grouped these into pedagogical AI tools versus generative AI tools.

The population represented across the reviewed studies spans primary/elementary students, middle/high school students, university students, and adult learners, making the review cross-level rather than focused on one learner group. The context is mathematics education broadly, drawing on international studies from multiple countries, with China, the United States, and Spain contributing the largest shares. Because this is a review, there is no single implementation setting; included studies covered multiple educational contexts and tool types.

The main conclusions are that AI in mathematics education is most commonly studied at the secondary level, with chatbots, AR/VR tools, and adaptive systems emerging as prominent categories. The authors conclude that AI shows strong potential to support personalized learning, feedback, engagement, and visualization of mathematical concepts, while also identifying future directions such as more longitudinal research, stronger attention to teacher-AI interaction, and continued development of commercially available tools for classroom use.

identified_tools.name: AI in mathematics education tools — pooled
identified_tools.description: Broad pooled category covering the range of AI and technology tools reviewed for mathematics education, including chatbots, adaptive learning systems/intelligent tutoring systems, virtual and augmented reality, learning analytics, serious games, and AI math problem solvers.
identified_tools.use_case: Systematic review of 32 studies (2019-2024) on mathematics education across primary, middle/high school, university, and adult learner contexts; synthesized studies using diverse AI tools rather than comparing against a single common control condition.

findings.finding_summary: The review reports that AI in mathematics education is associated with improved mathematics learning and achievement across the included literature. Adaptive learning systems, intelligent tutoring systems, chatbots, AR/VR tools, and related applications are described as enhancing learning outcomes, though no pooled quantitative effect size is reported.

The thematic synthesis states that AR/VR applications in mathematics education showed promising results for increasing students’ motivation, and AI-driven feedback systems and chatbots were reported to help reduce math anxiety. These are narrative review conclusions without pooled effect estimates.

The review identifies evidence from included studies that AR/VR-supported mathematics learning can improve problem-solving skills. This conclusion is presented as a thematic trend across the reviewed literature rather than as a pooled meta-analytic estimate.

identified_tools.name: Chatbots — pooled
identified_tools.description: Pooled category of AI chatbot tools used in mathematics education to provide conversational assistance, explanations, and interactive support.
identified_tools.use_case: Systematic review synthesis of mathematics education studies using chatbot tools (reported frequency N=9 studies/tools appearances), across university and adult learner contexts and some mixed deployments; no single comparison condition reported across the pool.

findings.finding_summary: The review states that chatbot-related AI systems are among the tools reported as enhancing mathematics education and improving learning outcomes. This is a narrative synthesis finding with no pooled effect size.

The thematic analysis reports that chatbot-related AI systems can reduce math anxiety in mathematics education. The paper presents this as an emergent trend from reviewed studies rather than a quantified pooled estimate.

identified_tools.name: Virtual reality — pooled
identified_tools.description: Pooled category of virtual reality tools used in mathematics education to create immersive, interactive learning environments for mathematical concepts and tasks.
identified_tools.use_case: Systematic review synthesis of mathematics education studies using VR tools (reported frequency N=7 studies/tools appearances), mainly in primary and middle/high school settings; no uniform comparison condition across studies.

findings.finding_summary: The review reports that the growing use of VR in mathematics education has shown promising results in enhancing students’ motivation. This is a thematic synthesis statement and does not include a pooled effect size.

The thematic analysis indicates that VR use in mathematics education has shown promising results for improving students’ problem-solving skills. The paper does not report a quantitative pooled estimate for this outcome.

identified_tools.name: Augmented reality — pooled
identified_tools.description: Pooled category of augmented reality tools used in mathematics education to overlay interactive digital representations onto real-world learning activities.
identified_tools.use_case: Systematic review synthesis of mathematics education studies using AR tools (reported frequency N=6 studies/tools appearances), primarily in middle/high school and some primary contexts; no common comparator across studies.

findings.finding_summary: The review reports that AR in mathematics education has shown promising results in enhancing students’ motivation. This is presented as a thematic finding from recent studies rather than a pooled quantitative result.
The review identifies AR use as showing promising results for strengthening students’ problem-solving skills in mathematics learning. No pooled effect size or confidence interval is reported.

identified_tools.name: Intelligent tutoring systems / adaptive learning systems
identified_tools.description: Pooled category covering intelligent tutoring systems and adaptive learning systems that personalize mathematics instruction, pacing, feedback, and task difficulty based on learner performance.
identified_tools.use_case: Systematic review synthesis of mathematics education studies using adaptive learning systems and ITS (reported frequency N=6 studies/tools appearances) across primary, middle/high school, university, and adult learner settings; no single shared comparison condition.

findings.finding_summary: The review reports that adaptive learning systems and intelligent tutoring systems are among the AI approaches associated with enhanced mathematics learning and achievement in the literature reviewed. The paper references their personalized learning and adaptive feedback functions but does not provide pooled effect sizes.

identified_tools.name: Learning analytics — pooled
identified_tools.description: Pooled category of AI-based learning analytics tools used in mathematics education to analyze learner data, interaction patterns, or emotional/behavioral indicators for educational insight and support.
identified_tools.use_case: Systematic review synthesis of mathematics education studies using learning analytics tools (reported frequency N=5 studies/tools appearances), including university and high school contexts; no common comparator reported.

findings.finding_summary: The review states that AI-driven analytics and feedback systems are significantly enhancing mathematics education and improving learning outcomes. This is reported thematically across included studies, without pooled numerical estimates.

identified_tools.name: Serious games
identified_tools.description: Pooled category of AI-supported serious games for mathematics education that embed mathematical learning tasks in game-based interactive environments.
identified_tools.use_case: Systematic review synthesis of mathematics education studies using serious games (reported frequency N=1 study/tool appearance) in high school settings; comparison condition not summarized at the category level.

identified_tools.name: AI-based mathematics problem solver — pooled
identified_tools.description: Pooled category of AI mathematics problem-solving tools that generate solutions or guidance for mathematical problems.
identified_tools.use_case: Systematic review synthesis of mathematics education studies using AI math problem solvers (reported frequency N=1 study/tool appearance), identified in high school context; no category-level comparison condition summarized.

identified_tools.name: ALEKS
identified_tools.description: Adaptive online learning platform for mathematics that assesses student knowledge and delivers individualized practice and instruction.
identified_tools.use_case: Mentioned in the literature review as one of the widely used Intelligent Tutoring Systems highlighted by Niño-Rojas et al. (2024). The review uses it as an example of a named ITS in mathematics learning, but does not analyze a primary study of ALEKS within this review's 32 included studies.

identified_tools.use_case: Mentioned in the literature review as one of the widely used ITS identified by Niño-Rojas et al. (2024). It is cited as prior-review context rather than as a tool evaluated in this review's included studies.

identified_tools.name: GeoGebra Tutor

identified_tools.use_case: Mentioned in the literature review as one of the ITS highlighted by Niño-Rojas et al. (2024). The present review does not report tool-specific outcomes for it.

identified_tools.description: A graded teaching system used in primary mathematics/STEAM learning.
identified_tools.use_case: Listed in Table 4 under Adaptive Learning/ITS for primary school use in China. It is not marked as commercialized and no tool-specific outcomes are synthesized.

identified_tools.name: Squirrel AI
identified_tools.description: An adaptive learning platform that personalizes mathematics education by adjusting task difficulty based on learner performance.
identified_tools.use_case: Listed in Table 4 under Adaptive Learning/ITS for middle school use in China and marked as commercialized. Table 5 identifies it as a pedagogical AI tool used for adaptive learning and personalized feedback.

identified_tools.name: e-Mathematics Learning Strategies Intelligent Assessment
identified_tools.description: An intelligent assessment system for mathematics learning strategies.
identified_tools.use_case: Listed in Table 4 under Adaptive Learning/ITS for high school use in China. The review provides no additional tool-specific results.

identified_tools.name: Khan Academy
identified_tools.description: Mastery-based online learning platform that provides instructional content, practice, progress tracking, and personalized pacing across subjects, including mathematics.
identified_tools.use_case: Listed in Table 4 under Adaptive Learning/ITS for adult learners in the United States. Table 5 describes it as covering mathematics from basic arithmetic to advanced calculus and linear algebra. Although Table 4 marks commercialization inconsistently, the review discusses it as a pedagogical AI tool used for adaptive learning support.

identified_tools.name: Game Gea2
identified_tools.description: A serious game used for mathematics learning.
identified_tools.use_case: Listed in Table 4 under Serious Games for high school use in Spain. The discussion notes that AI in serious games was the least represented category, with this area appearing in a 2021 study.

identified_tools.name: MathBot
identified_tools.description: A mathematics chatbot used to support learners through conversational interaction.
identified_tools.use_case: Listed in Table 4 under Chatbot for adult learners in the United States. The review names it as one of the identified AIME chatbots but does not provide a tool-specific effect summary.

identified_tools.name: SnatchBot
identified_tools.description: A chatbot platform that can be used to create educational bots, including bots for mathematics help.
identified_tools.use_case: Listed in Table 4 under Chatbot for university use in Spain and marked as commercialized. Table 5 describes it as a platform for creating educational bots that help students with math problems through conversational interfaces.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: Generative AI chatbot that produces and revises natural-language text, answers prompts, and provides writing support through conversational interaction.
identified_tools.use_case: Listed in Table 4 under Chatbot for university and adult learner contexts in the United States and marked as commercialized. Table 5 describes it as assisting math education by explaining mathematical concepts and solving problems through step-by-step guidance in conversational form. In the discussion, it is also grouped among generative AI tools providing instant assistance and personalized explanations.

identified_tools.name: Bard
identified_tools.description: A generative AI assistant that can produce explanations and educational content.
identified_tools.use_case: Listed in Table 4 under Chatbot for university use in the United States and marked as commercialized. Table 5 says it is generally used for content generation and can be adapted for educational purposes such as creating math problem sets or explanations.

identified_tools.name: Mobile Math Trails App
identified_tools.description: A mobile application for mathematics learning activities, likely supporting contextualized math trails.
identified_tools.use_case: Listed in Table 4 under Augmented Reality for middle school use in Indonesia. No further functionality or findings are specified in the review.

identified_tools.name: Zappar
identified_tools.description: An augmented reality app used to create interactive learning experiences by overlaying digital information on the real world.
identified_tools.use_case: Listed in Table 4 under Augmented Reality for middle school use in Saudi Arabia and marked as commercialized. Table 5 describes it as enabling engaging and interactive math learning experiences via AR.

identified_tools.use_case: Listed in Table 4 as an Augmented Reality tool for primary school in Cyprus and also noted by the review as categorizable as both AR and VR. Marked as commercialized. Table 5 describes it as a content creation tool for immersive and interactive math lessons.

identified_tools.name: cleARmaths
identified_tools.description: An augmented reality application focused on visualizing mathematical concepts.
identified_tools.use_case: Listed in Table 4 under Augmented Reality for high school use in Portugal and marked as commercialized. Table 5 says it focuses on AR applications in math education to visualize complex mathematical concepts.

identified_tools.name: Vlab

identified_tools.name: 3D Minigames

The review enumerates included minigames such as Multiplication board, Fractions Line Up, Declare a Fraction War, Fraction Hopscotch, Quadratic Function Analyzer, Linear Function Analyzer, Radians Conversion Code Colouring, Degrees Conversion Code Colouring, Polygon Party, Cartesian Battleship, The Scale factor, Fill'er Up (Liquid Measurement), and Connecting Europe.

identified_tools.use_case: Listed in Table 4 under Virtual Reality for university use in the United States and marked as commercialized. Table 5 describes it as making complex calculus more accessible and engaging through interaction with 3D concepts in VR.

identified_tools.name: Eclipse VR

identified_tools.use_case: Listed in Table 4 under Virtual Reality for primary school use in China and marked as commercialized. Table 5 notes its potential for geometry and spatial visualization learning environments.

identified_tools.name: NeoTrie VR
identified_tools.description: A virtual reality geometry tool for creating and interacting with 3D geometric figures.
identified_tools.use_case: Listed in Table 4 under Virtual Reality for primary school use in Spain and marked as commercialized. Table 5 says it enhances understanding of volume, area, and related properties through 3D geometric interaction.

identified_tools.name: Forum Graph
identified_tools.description: A Moodle-based graphing/analytics tool used to visualize or analyze learner interactions and mathematical learning data.
identified_tools.use_case: Listed in Table 4 as 'Forum Graph (moodle)' under Learning Analytics for high school use in Italy and also counted among university-level tools. Marked as commercialized. Table 5 characterizes it as a tool for creating graphs and charts that can support teaching of statistical and algebraic concepts.

identified_tools.name: GeoGebra
identified_tools.description: Dynamic mathematics software integrating geometry, algebra, graphing, spreadsheets, statistics, and calculus.
identified_tools.use_case: Listed in Table 4 under Learning Analytics, with use at primary and middle school levels across Israel, Germany, and the United States, and also mentioned among high-school tools. Marked as commercialized. The review also notes earlier mention of 'GeoGebra' in prior ITS reviews, and Table 5 describes its broad dynamic mathematics functionality.

identified_tools.name: Photomath
identified_tools.description: A smartphone-based math problem solver that scans problems and provides step-by-step solutions.
identified_tools.use_case: Listed in Table 4 under AI Math Problem Solver for high school use in the Philippines and marked as commercialized. Table 5 describes scanning and solving problems with step-by-step explanations. The discussion says mathematics problem solver apps like Photomath are practical for school students because they provide quick solutions, but are currently limited to straightforward problems and are more suitable for algebra-related questions than word problems.

findings.finding_summary: The review states that Photomath-like mathematics problem solver applications are practical for school students because they provide quick solutions to mathematical problems.

The review notes a limitation that mathematics problem solver applications such as Photomath are currently restricted to straightforward mathematical problems and are more suitable for algebra-related questions than word problems.

identified_tools.name: Fidgety Speech Emotion Recognition
identified_tools.description: A learning analytics/speech emotion recognition system used to analyze learner affect or speech-related signals.
identified_tools.use_case: Listed in Table 4 under Learning Analytics for university use in China. It is not marked as commercialized and no further details are provided.

identified_tools.name: Aurasma
identified_tools.description: An augmented reality platform; in the review it appears as the alternate name for HP Reveal.
identified_tools.use_case: Mentioned in Table 4 as 'HP Reveal (Aurasma)'. Included here because the review explicitly names the alternate branded product name.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed systematic review, which places it above primary correlational work, but it is not a meta-analysis with pooled effect sizes and does not present the full features needed for the highest evidence tier.
impact_tier_rationale: The review synthesizes generally positive findings about AI in mathematics education, but it does not report a pooled effect size or a clear quantified magnitude of impact, so overall impact remains promising but unclear.
